groups.summary: Every diagnostic the engine reports while it lowers sz.
Emitted classes this project's Tailwind generates no CSS for.
Opacity modifiers on a colour whose theme value color-mix() cannot dim.
Values that emit a class setting another property than their key sets.
Theme tokens whose name a built-in utility also uses.
sz keys the build removed because a later key in the same object covers them.
className classes the build removed because an sz class on the element covers them.

diagnostics.summary: A key no sz table knows, likely a typo.
diagnostics.text: `{key}` is not an sz property.
diagnostics.help: {spellingHint}; for a custom utility, define it with Tailwind's `@utility`.
diagnostics.note: the class is still emitted, and it styles nothing unless Tailwind serves that utility.

diagnostics.summary: An alias of a key, with the canonical spelling to write.

text.alias: `{key}` is an alias of `{canonical}`, and nothing is emitted for it.
text.font: `{key}` is not an sz key, and nothing is emitted for it.
text.scrollbar-color: `{key}` is not an sz key, and nothing is emitted for it.

help.font: write `weight` for the font weight, or `fontFamily` for the font family.
help.scrollbar-color: write `scrollbarThumb` for the thumb colour, or `scrollbarTrack` for the track colour.

diagnostics.summary: A key that was removed or replaced, with what to write instead.

text.runtime-alias: `{key}` is an alias of `{canonical}`, and nothing is emitted for its runtime value.
text.sugar-replaced: `{key}` was replaced, and nothing is emitted for it.
text.sugar: The boolean shorthand `{key}` was removed, and nothing is emitted for it.
text.removed: `{key}` was removed, and nothing is emitted for it.
text.replaced: `{key}` was replaced, and nothing is emitted for it.

help.runtime-alias: write the values {canonicalAllowed} on `{canonical}`, and any other value on its own key: {groups}.

diagnostics.summary: A numeric key, the mark of an array or spread passed as an sz object.
diagnostics.text: `sz` received a numeric key `{key}`, and its value is ignored.
diagnostics.help: pass an object of sz keys here; a numeric key usually means an array or a spread was passed in its place.

diagnostics.summary: A value a closed-enum key does not take.

text.sibling-group: `{key}: '{value}'` is not a `{key}` value; its class `{bare}` belongs to `{ {groupKey}: {groupLiteral} }`.
text.css-value: `{key}: '{value}'` is a CSS value, and `{key}-{value}` produces no CSS.
text.font-style: `{key}: '{value}'` has no Tailwind class, and nothing is emitted for it.
text.font-smoothing: `{key}: '{value}'` has no Tailwind class, and nothing is emitted for it.

help.sibling-group: write `{ {groupKey}: {groupLiteral} }`, so it combines with the other groups instead of resetting them.
help.font-style: use `'italic'` or `'normal'`; for any other style, such as oblique, write `css: { fontStyle: '{value}' }`.

note.dead: the class `{bare}` is still emitted, and only the CSS that Tailwind or your own stylesheet defines for it applies.

diagnostics.summary: A colour key given its opacity in a string, which emits nothing; the object form takes it.
diagnostics.text: `{key}: '{color}/{opacity}'` emits nothing: a string value cannot carry a slash opacity.
diagnostics.help: use the object form: `{ color: '{color}', op: {opacity} }`.

diagnostics.summary: A spacing value off Tailwind's quarter-step scale.
diagnostics.text: `{key}: {value}` is not on Tailwind's spacing scale, so the class produces no CSS.
diagnostics.help: use a quarter step such as `1.25`, `1.5` or `1.75`, or a unit value such as `'{value}rem'`.

diagnostics.summary: A font weight written as a numeric string.
diagnostics.text: `weight: '{value}'` is a numeric string, so `font-{value}` produces no CSS.
diagnostics.help: write `weight: {value}` as a number; it emits `font-[{value}]`.

diagnostics.summary: A border style on one side, which Tailwind cannot express.
diagnostics.text: `{key}: '{value}'` emits nothing: Tailwind has no per-side border style.
diagnostics.help: use `borderStyle: '{value}'` for every side, or a number on `{key}` for the width.

diagnostics.summary: An object on a key that names a property, not a variant.
diagnostics.text: `{key}` sets a property and is not a variant, so its object `{ {nestedKeys} }` emits `{key}:*` classes that produce no CSS.
diagnostics.help: move the nested keys up a level; for colour opacity, write `{ color: '…', op: … }`.

diagnostics.summary: An object on a csszyx-owned key that is not a variant.
diagnostics.text: `{key}` is not a variant, so its object emits `{key}:` classes that produce no CSS.
diagnostics.help: a `--*` key takes a declaration value; `container` takes `true`.

diagnostics.summary: A field a structured value (a mask layer) does not take.
diagnostics.text: `{owner}` has no field `{member}`, and nothing is emitted for it.
diagnostics.help: `{owner}` takes `{ {allowed} }`.

diagnostics.summary: A runtime value on a key with no CSS-variable utility.
diagnostics.text: `{key}` cannot take a runtime value: Tailwind has no utility for this key that reads a CSS variable.
diagnostics.help: name the values with `szv()`, or use `dynamic()` for open-ended data.
diagnostics.note: no class or variable is emitted for `{key}`.

diagnostics.summary: A spread in an sz object the build cannot resolve.
diagnostics.text: This `sz` object spreads a value the build cannot read, so the object falls back to the runtime.
diagnostics.help: use the array form: `sz={[x, { … }]}` in place of `sz={{ ...x, … }}`.
diagnostics.note: the classes of the spread value were not collected, so they produce no CSS unless another source names them.

diagnostics.summary: A props spread that may override the style sz emits.
diagnostics.text: This element spreads props that may carry `style`, and the `style` that `sz` writes can replace it.
diagnostics.help: move the spread `style` to an explicit `style` prop, so csszyx merges both values.

diagnostics.summary: An szs slot map the build cannot read, or one on a host element.

text.host-element: `szs` has no effect on a host element; it maps the slot names of a custom component.
text.unreadable-slot: A slot value in `szs` could not be read at build time, so no slot classes were compiled.

help.host-element: remove `szs`, or move it to the custom component whose slots it names.
help.unreadable-slot: write every slot as an identifier key with a static object literal or class string; for a value known only at runtime, pass the class string `dynamic()` returns.

diagnostics.note: the attribute is left unchanged.

diagnostics.summary: An szRecover value the build cannot read.
diagnostics.note: no `data-sz-recovery-token` is written for this element.

diagnostics.summary: A runtime className beside sz, which sz overrides.
diagnostics.text: `sz` wins over the runtime `className` on this element in any attribute order, so a caller's `className` cannot override these styles.
diagnostics.help: state the order in one `sz` array: `sz={[{ … }, className]}` for the caller to win, `sz={[className, { … }]}` for these styles to win.

diagnostics.summary: An element with more than one sz attribute, merged in order.
diagnostics.text: `<{elementName}>` carries {count} `sz` attributes, merged in order as `sz={[first, …, last]}`: the later one wins for each property.
diagnostics.help: fold them into one `sz` array, so the order is written down.

diagnostics.summary: Class names and sz on more than one side of a spread.
diagnostics.text: `<{elementName}>` has class names or `sz` on more than one side of a spread; in React, Preact, Solid and Qwik the last class attribute replaces the others, so {earlier} will not apply there.
diagnostics.help: write them in one `sz` array after {spreadPlace}, in the order that should win: `sz={[{example}]}`.
diagnostics.note: in Vue JSX every class is merged, so every side applies there.

diagnostics.summary: A value that moved to another key, with the key to write.

text.value: `{key}: '{value}'` moved to `{movedKey}`, and nothing is emitted for it.
text.mask-layer: `mask: '{value}'` names a gradient layer, which moved to `{layerKey}`, and nothing is emitted for it.

help.mask-layer: write this layer on `{layerKey}`; `mask` takes only `none`, a `url()` or a CSS variable.

diagnostics.summary: A stand-alone keyword written before a group key that replaces it.
diagnostics.text: `{global}: {valueLiteral}` comes before `{group}` in one sz object, so `{group}` replaces it and the `{global}` value styles nothing.
diagnostics.help: to override the group, layer it: `sz={[base, { {global}: {valueLiteral} }]}`.
diagnostics.note: a spread such as `{ ...base, {global}: {valueLiteral} }` keeps the same key order, so it does not fix this.

diagnostics.summary: A runtime value beside the other side of its key family.
diagnostics.text: `{key}` takes a runtime value beside `{other}` in one sz object, so both classes can be emitted and Tailwind's stylesheet order decides which applies, whatever the object's order.

diagnostics.summary: A runtime fallback whose classes were never collected.

text.szv: The `szv` config cannot be read at build time: {fallbackReason}.

help.szv: pass the config inline, or as a module-level const object literal.

note.sz: its classes were not collected, so they produce no CSS unless another source names them.
note.szr: its classes were not collected, so they produce no CSS unless another source names them.
note.szv: none of its variant classes were collected, so they produce no CSS unless another source names them.

diagnostics.summary: A runtime fallback whose classes were still collected.

text.sz-array-element: This `sz` array element is an object literal with a runtime value, so the whole element is resolved at runtime.

help.sz-array-element: use finite literal ternary branches where you can, or move the runtime values to `dynamic()`.

note.sz: the runtime still turns the value into classes.
note.sz-array-element: its classes are still collected, best-effort.

diagnostics.summary: A merge table this engine cannot read, so nothing merged.

text.unreadable: The merge table is not one this engine reads ({error}), so the build removes no class that a later sz key covers.
text.format-mismatch: The merge table is in format {tableFormat}, and this csszyx version reads format {mergeTableFormat}, so the build removes no class that a later sz key covers.

diagnostics.help: install the same csszyx version of every `@csszyx` package, then rebuild; under Turbopack, delete `.csszyx/merge-table.json` and run `csszyx next prebuild`.
diagnostics.note: every class is kept, as before 0.18, so `{ pb: 2, p: 4 }` emits both and the stylesheet order decides.

diagnostics.summary: A file the parser rejected, which contributes no classes.

text.summary: This file could not be parsed (syntax errors: {errorCount}).
text.panicked: The parser stopped at a syntax error it could not recover from.
text.expression: This `sz` value could not be parsed as a JavaScript expression.
text.prescan: The prescan could not parse this file, so none of its classes reached the safelist.

help.syntax: fix the syntax at this position.
help.summary: fix the syntax errors reported for this file.
help.panicked: fix the syntax error reported for this file.
help.expression: write the value as an object literal, such as `{ p: 4 }`.
help.prescan: fix the syntax error, or check that the file extension matches its contents.

note.expression: the attribute is left as written, and no class is generated for it.
note.prescan: its classes produce no CSS unless another source names them.

diagnostics.summary: A file nested deeper than the parser guard allows.
diagnostics.text: Source nesting exceeds {maxNestingDepth} levels (found {depth}).
diagnostics.help: flatten the structure; nesting this deep usually comes from `sz` or JSX over-nested by hand or by generated code.
diagnostics.note: the file is left unchanged and contributes no classes.

diagnostics.summary: An sz attribute whose value the engine cannot read.
diagnostics.text: This `sz` attribute has no value, or a JSX element as its value.
diagnostics.help: give `sz` a value in braces, such as `sz={{ p: 4 }}`, or remove it.
diagnostics.note: the attribute is left as written; the rest of the file is still transformed.

diagnostics.summary: A file over the AST budget, left unchanged.

text.transform: This file exceeds the AST node budget.
text.prescan: The prescan skipped this file because it exceeds the AST node budget, so none of its classes reached the safelist.

diagnostics.help: split the file, or raise `build.astBudgetLimit` in the plugin options; the Turbopack loader takes no budget option, so split the file there.

note.transform: the file is left unchanged, and none of its classes are collected.
note.prescan: its classes produce no CSS unless another source names them.

diagnostics.summary: A CSS variable mangleVars could not hoist to a component.

text.no-lca: `mangleVars` did not hoist `{name}`: its {usageCount} usages share no common JSX ancestor.
text.non-host-ancestor: `mangleVars` did not hoist `{name}`: the common ancestor of its {usageCount} usages cannot take a `style` prop.
text.max-depth: `mangleVars` did not hoist `{name}`: one of its {usageCount} usages sits more than {maxDepth} levels below their common ancestor.

diagnostics.note: each element that uses it keeps its own scoped variable, and every class is still emitted.

diagnostics.summary: A colour object with a slash opacity in `color`; the object takes it in `op`.

text.op-given: `{key}: { color: '{base}/{opacity}{important}', op: {op} }` sets opacity twice; a colour object takes its opacity in `op`, not in `color`.
text.op-absent: `{key}: { color: '{base}/{opacity}{important}' }` puts the opacity in `color`; a colour object takes it in `op`.

note.op-given: the class uses `op: {op}`; the `/{opacity}` in `color` is ignored.

diagnostics.summary: A value wrapped in the brackets or parentheses csszyx writes itself.
diagnostics.text: `{key}: '{value}'` wraps its value in brackets or parentheses, which csszyx writes itself, so nothing is emitted for it.
diagnostics.help: write `{key}: '{inner}'`; grid line names at both ends, such as `[a] 1fr [b]`, go in `css: { … }`.

diagnostics.summary: An `op` that is not a number from 0 to 100, or one below 1 that reads as a fraction.

text.range: `{key}: { op: {op} }` is not a number from 0 to 100, so the colour is written without an opacity.
text.fraction: `{key}: { op: {op} }` is {op}% opacity: `op` is a percent, not a fraction of 1.

help.range: write `op` as a number from `0` to `100`, such as `op: 50` or `op: 33.3`.

diagnostics.summary: A negative value on a key Tailwind serves no negative utility for.
diagnostics.text: `{className}` produces no CSS: this project's Tailwind serves `{utility}` but no negative form of it.
diagnostics.help: drop the sign, or define the negative with Tailwind's `@utility`; `csszyx check --rule unsigned-value` lists every one.
diagnostics.note: the class is still emitted, and it styles nothing.

diagnostics.summary: A CSS-wide keyword on a served class that no property it sets takes.
diagnostics.text: `{className}` sets no property to `{keyword}`: this project's Tailwind writes the keyword into a custom property or inside another value.
diagnostics.help: set the CSS property to `'{keyword}'` in `css: { … }`; `csszyx check --rule inert-keyword` lists every one.
diagnostics.note: the class is still emitted, and it styles nothing.

diagnostics.summary: An emitted class this project's Tailwind generates no CSS for.
diagnostics.text: `{className}` produces no CSS: this project's Tailwind serves no such utility.
diagnostics.help: fix the sz key or value, or define the class with Tailwind's `@utility`; `csszyx check --rule dead-class` lists every one.
diagnostics.note: the class is still emitted, and it styles nothing.

diagnostics.summary: Tailwind entries in one project that set different prefixes.
diagnostics.text: The Tailwind stylesheets of this project set different prefixes ({entries}), so no class csszyx emits is served by all of them.

help.build: give every Tailwind stylesheet the same `@import "tailwindcss"` line, or list the stylesheets this build loads with {setting}.
help.next: give every Tailwind stylesheet the same `@import "tailwindcss"` line, list the stylesheets this build loads with {setting}, or leave another app's directory out with {ignoreSetting}.
help.check: give every Tailwind stylesheet the same `@import "tailwindcss"` line.

note.build: no module was transformed, and nothing was written.
note.next: no module was transformed, and nothing was written.
note.check: the dead-class check did not run.

diagnostics.summary: A value that emits a class setting another property than its key sets.
diagnostics.text: `{key}: '{value}'` emits `{className}`, which sets {sets}, not the property `{key}` sets.
diagnostics.help: move the value to the key that sets {sets}, or declare a theme token named `{value}` if the spelling was deliberate.
diagnostics.note: `{className}` produces CSS, so no other check reports it.

diagnostics.summary: An opacity modifier on a colour whose theme value color-mix() cannot dim.
diagnostics.text: `{className}` carries an opacity modifier that does not apply: its theme token resolves to the bare comma triplet `{value}`, which `color-mix()` cannot dim.
diagnostics.help: wrap the token's variable in a colour function, such as `rgb(var(--your-triplet))`.

diagnostics.summary: A bare variant name Tailwind serves no variant for, on a utility it serves.
diagnostics.text: `{className}` produces no CSS: Tailwind serves no `{variant}` variant.

help.attribute-or-aria: write `{ '[{variant}]': { … } }` to match the HTML attribute, or `aria: { {variant}: { … } }` for the ARIA state.
help.unknown: check the spelling of `{variant}`; a camelCase key is written in kebab-case.
help.container-name: write `{ '{query}/{variant}': { … } }` for a container named `{variant}`; a name under a query is a variant.

diagnostics.note: the class is still emitted, and it styles nothing unless the project defines `{variant}` with `@custom-variant`.

diagnostics.summary: A theme token whose name a built-in utility also uses.

text.classes: Theme token `{name}` also names `{classes}`, so Tailwind compiles both meanings into one rule, which sets the token's property and the built-in's.
text.utility-keyword: Theme token `{name}` shadows a built-in utility keyword, so Tailwind compiles both meanings into one class, which sets the token's property and the built-in's.
text.value: Theme token `{name}` shadows a built-in value, so Tailwind compiles both meanings into one class, which sets the token's property and the built-in's.

diagnostics.help: rename the token; while it shares a built-in name, no class order or `szcn` call can fix this.
diagnostics.note: a later class that sets only one of them does not replace it in `szcn`, so both apply and stylesheet order decides which wins; `classify` reports the built-in meaning only.

diagnostics.summary: An sz key the build removed because a later key in the same object covers it.
diagnostics.text: The build removes `{className}`, written as `{key}`, because a later key in the same sz object sets every property it sets.
diagnostics.help: delete `{key}` from the object; to keep every covered class, set `build.mergeCoveredClasses: false` in the plugin options.

diagnostics.summary: A className class the build removed because an sz class on the element covers it.
diagnostics.text: The build removes `{className}` from `className`, because an `sz` class on the same element sets every property it sets.
diagnostics.help: delete `{className}` from `className`; to keep every covered class, set `build.mergeCoveredClasses: false` in the plugin options.

diagnostics.summary: A recovery manifest that is not valid JSON or not in the recovery format.

text.json: The recovery manifest on this page is not valid JSON, so it is ignored.
text.format: This recovery manifest is missing the field(s) `{missing}`, so `parseManifest` cannot read it.
text.parse: This recovery manifest is not valid JSON, so `parseManifest` cannot read it.

help.json: serve the HTML as the build wrote it; the manifest is the `__SZ_RECOVERY_MANIFEST__` script the build adds to the page.
help.format: pass the manifest the build wrote, unchanged.
help.parse: pass the manifest the build wrote, unchanged.

diagnostics.summary: A mangle map on the page that is not a plain map of class names, so it is ignored.

text.schema: The class census on this page (`__CSSZYX_MANGLE_MAP__`) is not a map of class names to class names, so it is ignored.
text.json: The class census on this page (`__CSSZYX_MANGLE_MAP__`) is not valid JSON, so it is ignored.

diagnostics.help: serve the HTML as the build wrote it; a census that cannot be read means the page was changed or cut short after the build.

diagnostics.summary: A mangle census on the page that is not a valid map, so nothing was verified.
diagnostics.text: The class census on this page could not be read, so the mangle checksum was not verified.
diagnostics.help: serve the HTML as the build wrote it; the line before this one says what is wrong with the census.

diagnostics.summary: A mangle map whose hash differs from the checksum it was built with.
diagnostics.text: The mangle map on this page hashes to `{computed}`, and the checksum it was built with is `{expected}`, so the check fails.
diagnostics.help: deploy the HTML and the bundle from one build.
diagnostics.note: this detects a damaged or stale page, not an attacker; the checksum is not signed.

diagnostics.summary: A page with a mangle checksum but no census or map to recompute it from.
diagnostics.text: This page carries the checksum `{checksum}` but neither a class census nor a bundled mangle map to recompute it from, so nothing was verified.
diagnostics.help: keep `production.hydrationCensus` on, its default, when the build sets `production.mangleVars` without `production.mangle`, since such a build bundles no map; otherwise, load the bundle that registers the map on this page.

diagnostics.summary: A page without Web Crypto, so the mangle checksum cannot be recomputed.
diagnostics.text: Web Crypto is unavailable, so csszyx cannot recompute the mangle checksum.
diagnostics.help: serve the page over HTTPS, or from `localhost`.
diagnostics.note: `crypto.subtle` exists only in a secure context; `verifyMangleChecksumAsync` answers `false` without checking.

diagnostics.summary: A hydration check that threw on an element and stopped.

text.checksum-mismatch: The HTML, the bundle and the recovery manifest do not all come from one build, so csszyx aborted hydration at `<{tagName}>`.
text.map-missing: Your code called `abortHydration` with `map_missing`, so csszyx aborted hydration at `<{tagName}>`.
text.invalid-token: Your code called `abortHydration` with `invalid_token`, so csszyx aborted hydration at `<{tagName}>`.

help.checksum-mismatch: deploy the HTML, the bundle and the manifest from one build.
help.map-missing: serve the page with the mangle map its build wrote.
help.invalid-token: deploy the HTML and the recovery manifest from one build.

note.checksum-mismatch: csszyx only marks the element with `data-sz-hydration-aborted` and `data-sz-interactive="false"`; nothing skips hydrating it unless your code checks `isHydrationAborted`.
note.map-missing: the caller reported: {message}; csszyx only marks the element, and nothing skips hydrating it unless your code checks `isHydrationAborted`.
note.invalid-token: the caller reported: {message}; csszyx only marks the element, and nothing skips hydrating it unless your code checks `isHydrationAborted`.

diagnostics.summary: A hydration mismatch on an element without an szRecover directive.
diagnostics.text: This element has a hydration mismatch but no `szRecover` directive, so it is not recovered on the client.
diagnostics.help: add `szRecover="csr"` to recover it, or `szRecover="dev-only"` to recover it in development only.

diagnostics.summary: An szRecover="dev-only" element in a production build, where its recovery is off.

text.runtime: This element has `szRecover="dev-only"`, which is off in production, so its hydration mismatch is not recovered.
text.stripped: The production manifest leaves out {count} `szRecover="dev-only"` token(s), so recovery for those elements is off in production.

help.runtime: fix the mismatch, or use `szRecover="csr"` where recovery must run in production.
help.stripped: use `szRecover="csr"` on any of them whose recovery must run in production.

note.stripped: this is expected in a production build; the tokens are at {sites}.

diagnostics.summary: A hydration mismatch the runtime recovered by rendering on the client.
diagnostics.text: The hydration-abort marks on this element were cleared, so your code can render it on the client.
diagnostics.help: fix the cause of the mismatch; with `szRecover="csr"`, this recovery also runs in production.

diagnostics.summary: A merge table in a format this runtime does not read, so szcn merges nothing.
diagnostics.text: The merge table was written in format {format}, and this csszyx version reads format {expected}, so `szcn` ignores the table and removes only exact repeats.
diagnostics.help: run the build, or `csszyx next prebuild` on Next.js, with the installed csszyx to write it again.

diagnostics.summary: A run with no merge table, so szcn removes only exact repeats.
diagnostics.text: `szcn` has no merge table in this run, so it removes only exact repeats: `szcn('p-2', 'p-4')` keeps both classes.
diagnostics.help: use the csszyx plugin for Vite, Rollup, webpack or Next.js, which registers one; for jest, run the build or `csszyx next prebuild` first.
diagnostics.note: the csszyx plugin registers no table under esbuild, Rspack, Rsbuild, Rolldown, Farm or Bun.

diagnostics.summary: A raw sz object that reached the runtime because its file was not compiled.
diagnostics.text: A raw `sz` object reached the runtime because its file was not compiled, so it produces no CSS.
diagnostics.help: add the package directory to `compileSources` when the file lives in a workspace package; otherwise, check that the bundler does not skip the file.
diagnostics.note: csszyx dropped the object, so the DOM does not get `sz="[object Object]"`.

diagnostics.summary: A registerSzcnGroups call, which no longer changes what szcn merges.
diagnostics.text: `registerSzcnGroups` no longer changes what `szcn` merges: `szcn` merges on the CSS your Tailwind compiles, and the groups you register only name the property that `classify` and `splitBox` read.
diagnostics.help: declare the tokens under `@theme` (`--color-*`, `--text-*`, `--font-*`, `--font-weight-*`), delete the CSS rules you wrote for those classes, and use a csszyx integration that supplies a merge table.
diagnostics.note: `szcn` never removes a class from `@utility`, a plugin or plain CSS; without a table it removes only exact repeats.

diagnostics.summary: A theme token defined under two namespaces that share one class prefix.

text.color-text-size: Theme token `{name}` is defined as both a colour and a text size, so `classify` cannot name the property of `text-{name}`, and Tailwind compiles that class for only one of them.
text.font-family-weight: Theme token `{name}` is defined as both a font family and a font weight, so `classify` cannot name the property of `font-{name}`, and Tailwind compiles that class for only one of them.

diagnostics.help: rename one of the tokens.

note.color-text-size: a `text:color` or `text:size` placement in `splitBox` does not match `text-{name}`; `szcn` merges on the compiled CSS and is not affected.
note.font-family-weight: a `font:family` or `font:weight` placement in `splitBox` does not match `font-{name}`; `szcn` merges on the compiled CSS and is not affected.

diagnostics.summary: A has/pick/omit selector that can never match a token.

text.array: `has`, `pick` and `omit` take one selector, so an array matches nothing.
text.empty: The empty selector `{}` names no category, so it matches nothing.
text.multi: An object selector names one category and value, so `{ {categories} }` can never match a single token.
text.property: `{property}` is not a property csszyx tells apart, so `{selector}` matches nothing.
text.sz-qualified: `{selector}` names a property, and `hasSz`, `pickSz` and `omitSz` match an sz key by category only, so it matches nothing.

help.array: pass the selectors one at a time; `splitBox` takes a list in `inner` and `outer`.
help.empty: name a category and a value, such as `{ overflow: "hidden" }`.
help.property: use one of `{properties}`; `classify('<a class>')` shows the one a class carries.

diagnostics.summary: A selector name that is no category or class prefix csszyx knows.
diagnostics.text: `{name}` is not a category or class prefix csszyx knows, so it matches nothing.

help.no-hint: call `classify('<a class>')` to see the category a class belongs to.
help.property-hint: use the category `{hint}`, or `{hint}:{name}` to match that property only.

diagnostics.summary: A splitBox placement written with a variant or marker, which never matches.
diagnostics.text: A `splitBox` placement list names a class by its base, so `{selector}` never matches: the variant prefix and the `!` or `-` marker are stripped before the comparison.
diagnostics.help: write `{ {side}: ['{base}'] }`; it places every variant of `{base}`.

diagnostics.summary: A peer class splitBox kept on the frame although its base belongs inside.
diagnostics.text: `splitBox` keeps `{token}` on the frame although `{base}` belongs inside, because a peer rule reaches siblings and the content node is a child of the frame, where it could never match.
diagnostics.help: target the content from the frame instead: `{reaching}`.

diagnostics.summary: A class or raw CSS splitBox cannot classify, placed on the fallback node.

text.class: `{token}` is not a utility csszyx knows, so it went to the {node} node with everything else it could not classify.
text.raw-css: The `css` key holds raw CSS `splitBoxSz` does not classify, so it went to the {node} node with everything else it could not classify.

help.class: if it belongs on the other node, place it there with `{ {side}: ['{token}'] }`; a custom `@utility` that sets properties of both nodes has no correct side, so split it into two utilities.
help.raw-css: if its declarations belong on the other node, place it yourself with `{ {side}: ['css'] }`.

diagnostics.summary: A scrolling content node whose height nothing bounds, so it grows instead.
diagnostics.text: `splitBox` put `{scroller}` on the content node, but nothing bounds the height of either node, so the content grows instead of scrolling.
diagnostics.help: give the className a height bound such as `h-64`, `max-h-96` or `h-full`, or put `flex flex-col min-h-0` on the frame and `flex-1 min-h-0` on the content.

diagnostics.summary: A rounded frame that does not clip its scrolling content.
diagnostics.text: The `splitBox` frame is rounded and the content scrolls, but the frame does not clip, so scrolled content paints over the corners.
diagnostics.help: add `overflow-hidden` to the frame.

diagnostics.summary: A hiding class placed on the content node, which leaves the frame visible.
diagnostics.text: `splitBox` put `{hidden}` on the content node, so the frame keeps its background, border and size and stays visible.
diagnostics.help: pass `{ outer: ['hidden'] }` if the whole box should disappear.

diagnostics.summary: A part of an szv config that does not have the shape szv reads.

text.config: The `szv` config is not an object (got {got}), so `szv` returns an empty sz object.
text.base: `base` in the `szv` config is not an sz object (got {got}), so `szv` ignores it.
text.variants: `variants` in the `szv` config is not an object (got {got}), so `szv` returns only `base`.
text.default-variants: `defaultVariants` in the `szv` config is not an object (got {got}), so no variant gets a default value.
text.dimension: `variants.{dimension}` is not an object of values (got {got}), so it adds no classes.
text.variant-value: `variants.{dimension}.{token}` is not an sz object (got {got}), so it is ignored.

help.config: pass an object such as `{ base: { … }, variants: { … } }`.
help.base: make `base` an sz object, such as `{ p: 4 }`.
help.variants: make `variants` an object of dimensions, such as `{ size: { sm: { p: 2 } } }`.
help.default-variants: make `defaultVariants` an object of values, such as `{ size: 'sm' }`.
help.dimension: make `variants.{dimension}` an object that maps each value to an sz object.
help.variant-value: make it an sz object, such as `{ p: 4 }`, or `null` to add nothing.

diagnostics.summary: An sz object at runtime nested deeper than the depth limit.

text.value: This `sz` value nests deeper than {maxDepth} levels, so csszyx rejects it.
text.szv-config: `{where}` in the `szv` config nests deeper than {maxDepth} levels, so `szv` rejects it at render.

help.value: check what reaches the `sz` prop; nesting this deep usually means untrusted or looping data.
help.szv-config: flatten `{where}`; nesting this deep usually means the config was built from untrusted or looping data.

diagnostics.summary: A key in an szv config that csszyx never reads, such as __proto__.
diagnostics.text: `{where}` in the `szv` config has the forbidden key `{key}`, so it is ignored.
diagnostics.help: remove the key; csszyx never reads `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`.

diagnostics.summary: A selection that names a variant the szv config does not declare.
diagnostics.text: The `szv` selection names the variant `{key}`, which `variants` does not declare, so it is ignored.
diagnostics.help: declare `variants.{key}`, or remove `{key}` from the selection.

diagnostics.summary: A selection that gives a variant a value it has no styles for.
diagnostics.text: The `szv` selection sets `{key}` to `{value}`, which `variants.{key}` does not define, so it adds no class.

help.listed: add `{value}` to `variants.{key}`, or use one of `{allowed}`.
help.none: add `{value}` to `variants.{key}`, which defines no value yet.

diagnostics.summary: An sz object from szv() used as a class string, which renders "[object Object]".
diagnostics.text: An sz object from `szv()` was used as a class string, such as `className={someSzv({ … })}`, which renders `[object Object]` in a production build.
diagnostics.help: pass it to an `sz` prop, or turn it into a class string with `szr(…)` first.
diagnostics.note: a development build renders an empty string in its place.

diagnostics.summary: A session in which dynamic() has injected so many classes the CSSOM keeps growing.
diagnostics.text: `dynamic()` has injected {count} or more unique classes this session, and injected CSS rules are never removed, so the CSSOM keeps growing and style recalculation slows.
diagnostics.help: drive continuously changing values, such as a width that changes every animation frame, through a CSS variable instead.

diagnostics.summary: An arbitrary value dynamic() dropped because it could inject CSS.
diagnostics.text: The arbitrary value in `{utility}` could inject CSS, so `dynamic()` omits the class.
diagnostics.help: keep untrusted data out of arbitrary values, or validate it before it reaches `dynamic()`.
diagnostics.note: only the first dropped value of a session is reported.

diagnostics.summary: A runtime value that is not a boolean on a key only a boolean can toggle.
diagnostics.text: The runtime value of `{key}` has type `{valueType}`, and only a boolean toggles this class, so it is omitted.
diagnostics.help: pass `true` or `false`; write other values as literals, or use `dynamic()` for a responsive object.

diagnostics.summary: A runtime value of a type no CSS value can be resolved from.
diagnostics.text: The runtime value of `{key}` has type `{valueType}`, which cannot be resolved to CSS, so the property is omitted.
diagnostics.help: pass a number, a token or a CSS length; for a responsive object, use `dynamic()`.

diagnostics.summary: A development warning with no source location; csszyx check names the file and key.
diagnostics.text: The `sz` key warning above has no source location, so it does not name the file that triggered it.
diagnostics.help: run `npx @csszyx/cli check` to list every file and key at once; set `CSSZYX_NO_PROJECT_SCAN_HINT=1` to hide this line.

diagnostics.summary: More findings of one kind than a run lists; the rest are counted, not printed.

text.dev-warnings: This session has printed {count} distinct development warnings, so further ones are suppressed.
text.unknown-keys: This process has reported {count} distinct unknown sz keys, so further ones are suppressed.
text.per-id: This build left {count} more `{id}` finding(s) unlisted.

help.dev-warnings: look above for one warning repeating with different values; a `className` built from data is the usual cause.
help.unknown-keys: look above for one key repeating with different names; sz keys built from data are the usual cause.

diagnostics.summary: An sz attribute string that does not parse.

text.char: The `sz` attribute `{input}` has an unexpected `{char}` at offset {index}, so the element gets no classes from it.
text.end: The `sz` attribute `{input}` ends at offset {index} before a key or value is complete, so the element gets no classes from it.

help.char: write it as an object literal with commas between keys, such as `sz="p: 4, w: '1/2'"`; quote a value that holds `/` or `#`.
help.end: give every key a `:` and a value, and close every `[` and quote, such as `sz="p: 4, [&>span]: { m: 2 }"`.

diagnostics.summary: An options argument that is not the one object the call takes.

text.transform: `transform` takes its options in one object, so a second argument that is not an object, or a third argument, is refused.
text.csszyx-turbopack: `csszyxTurbopack` takes one object, with the config to extend under `turbopack`, so a second argument is refused.
text.csszyx-turbopack-option: `csszyxTurbopack` has no option(s) `{options}`, so the call is refused.
text.class-name-to-sz-object: `classNameToSzObject` takes its options in one object, so a second argument that is not an object, or a third argument, is refused.
text.class-name-to-sz-object-option: `classNameToSzObject` has no option(s) `{options}`, so the call is refused.
text.serialize-manifest: `serializeManifest` takes its options in one object, so a second argument that is not an object, or a third argument, is refused.
text.migrate-source: `migrateSource` takes the path under `filename` in one options object, so a second argument without it, or a third argument, is refused.
text.engine-call: `{call}` takes its options in one object, so a second argument that is not an object, or a third argument, is refused.

help.transform: pass the prefix and the mangle map as keys: `transform(sz, { prefix: 'hover:', mangleMap })`.
help.csszyx-turbopack: write `csszyxTurbopack({ turbopack: <your config>, ...options })`; loader options go beside `turbopack`.
help.csszyx-turbopack-option: use `config`, `glob`, `importedStaticSz`, `mergeCoveredClasses`, `parserMode`, `safelistOutputFile`, `tailwindStylesheet` or `turbopack`; a Turbopack setting such as `rules` goes under `turbopack`.
help.class-name-to-sz-object: pass the migration map under `customMap`: `classNameToSzObject(className, { customMap })`.
help.class-name-to-sz-object-option: pass the migration map under `customMap`: `classNameToSzObject(className, { customMap })`.
help.serialize-manifest: pass the flag as a key: `serializeManifest(manifest, { pretty: true })`.
help.migrate-source: pass the path as a key beside the other options: `migrateSource(source, { filename: 'Card.tsx' })`.
help.engine-call: move every argument after the first into one object, as in `transformSource(source, { filename: 'Card.tsx' })` or `scanModuleLinks(files, { registryEntries, parser })`.

diagnostics.summary: An sz object passed to a string helper before the lowering module is loaded.
diagnostics.text: A string helper received an sz object, but the module that turns sz objects into class names is not loaded, so it cannot produce class names for it.
diagnostics.help: add `import '@csszyx/runtime/lowering';` once at startup when the code runs outside the csszyx bundler plugin, such as in unit tests or scripts; the plugin loads it for files that can pass objects at runtime.

diagnostics.summary: An sz object passed to a lite-runtime helper, which cannot lower objects.
diagnostics.text: `{fnName}()` takes class strings and received the plain object `{received}`, because the compiler could not resolve this `sz` prop at build time.
diagnostics.help: write `sz={[cond ? varA : varB, { key: 'val' }]}`; a spread of a conditional, such as `sz={{ ...(cond ? varA : varB), key: 'val' }}`, is the usual cause.
diagnostics.note: a production build skips this check: `_sz` returns the object, or `[object Object]` beside other classes, and `_szMerge` throws a `TypeError`.

diagnostics.summary: A class string passed to splitBoxSz, which takes sz objects.
diagnostics.text: `splitBoxSz` partitions sz objects, not class strings, so it cannot split `{value}`.
diagnostics.help: use `splitBox()` for a class string.
diagnostics.note: a production build drops the string instead of throwing.

diagnostics.summary: Two builds sharing one runtime that registered different Tailwind prefixes.

text.prefixes: Two builds sharing one JavaScript runtime registered the Tailwind prefixes `{first}` and `{second}`, so csszyx cannot tell which prefix their classes take.
text.unprefixed: Two builds sharing one JavaScript runtime registered different Tailwind prefixes, `{first}` and none, so csszyx cannot tell which prefix their classes take.

diagnostics.help: keep independently configured applications on separate `@csszyx/runtime` instances, or align their Tailwind prefix.

diagnostics.summary: A dynamic manifest the browser could not fetch.
diagnostics.text: The `dynamic()` manifest could not be fetched (HTTP status {status}), so every class is treated as new and injected at runtime.
diagnostics.help: serve the manifest at the URL `setManifestUrl` names, or turn `build.emitManifest` on.
diagnostics.note: the error is caught and nothing is printed; csszyx does not fetch it again this session until you call `resetManifest`.

diagnostics.summary: A native engine that is missing, cannot load, or predates this compiler.

text.no-platform-package: No prebuilt native engine covers `{platform}`, so the `rust` parser cannot run.
text.not-installed: `{packageName}` is not installed, so the `rust` parser cannot run.
text.missing-export: `{packageName}` does not export `{exportName}()`, which the installed `@csszyx/core` calls, so the `rust` parser cannot run.
text.stale-binding: `{packageName}` returns results the installed `@csszyx/core` cannot read, so the `rust` parser cannot run.
text.stale-binding-versions: `{packageName}` {nativeVersion} returns results the installed `@csszyx/core` {coreVersion} cannot read, so the `rust` parser cannot run.
text.wasm-fallback: The native engine is not available here, so the default `rust` parser runs on the wasm engine.

help.no-platform-package: set the parser to `wasm` (`build.parser: 'wasm'` in the plugin options, `parserMode: 'wasm'` in `csszyxTurbopack`, or `--parser-mode wasm` on `csszyx next`); the wasm engine ships inside `@csszyx/core`.
help.not-installed: reinstall without skipping optional dependencies, which installs `{packageName}` with `@csszyx/core`, or set the parser to `wasm` (`build.parser: 'wasm'` in the plugin options, `parserMode: 'wasm'` in `csszyxTurbopack`, or `--parser-mode wasm` on `csszyx next`).
help.missing-export: update `@csszyx/core` and `{packageName}` together, to the same version, or set the parser to `wasm` (`build.parser: 'wasm'` in the plugin options, `parserMode: 'wasm'` in `csszyxTurbopack`, or `--parser-mode wasm` on `csszyx next`).
help.stale-binding: update `@csszyx/core` and `{packageName}` together, to the same version, or set the parser to `wasm` (`build.parser: 'wasm'` in the plugin options, `parserMode: 'wasm'` in `csszyxTurbopack`, or `--parser-mode wasm` on `csszyx next`).
help.stale-binding-versions: update `@csszyx/core` and `{packageName}` together, to the same version, or set the parser to `wasm` (`build.parser: 'wasm'` in the plugin options, `parserMode: 'wasm'` in `csszyxTurbopack`, or `--parser-mode wasm` on `csszyx next`).
help.wasm-fallback: reinstall without skipping optional dependencies to get the native engine, or set `build.parser: 'wasm'` to hide this line.

diagnostics.note: the wasm engine produces the same output; only parsing is slower.

diagnostics.summary: A wasm engine that failed to load.
diagnostics.text: The wasm engine in `@csszyx/core` did not load, so the `wasm` parser cannot run.
diagnostics.help: reinstall `@csszyx/core`; the wasm engine ships inside it as `parser-wasm`.
diagnostics.note: the loader reported: {detail}.

diagnostics.summary: A native engine csszyx migrate needs and cannot load; migrate has no wasm lane.

text.no-platform-package: No prebuilt native engine covers `{platform}`, so migrate cannot run.
text.not-installed: `{packageName}` is not installed, so migrate cannot run.
text.missing-export: `{packageName}` predates migrate and does not export `{exportName}()`, so migrate cannot run.
text.stale-binding: `{packageName}` returns results the installed `@csszyx/core` cannot read, so migrate cannot run.
text.stale-binding-versions: `{packageName}` {nativeVersion} returns results the installed `@csszyx/core` {coreVersion} cannot read, so migrate cannot run.

help.no-platform-package: run migrate on Linux, macOS or Windows, on x64 or arm64, where a prebuilt native engine exists.
help.not-installed: reinstall without skipping optional dependencies, which installs `{packageName}` with `@csszyx/core`.
help.missing-export: update `@csszyx/core` and `{packageName}` together, to a version that carries migrate.
help.stale-binding: update `@csszyx/core` and `{packageName}` together, to the same version.
help.stale-binding-versions: update `@csszyx/core` and `{packageName}` together, to the same version.

diagnostics.note: no file was changed; migrate runs on the native engine only, and builds and the runtime do not need it.

diagnostics.summary: An engine built from other source than the compiler that loads it.

text.version: `@csszyx/compiler` {expectedVersion} loaded the {artifact} engine {foundVersion}, and the two must come from the same release, so csszyx stops.

text.unreported: `@csszyx/compiler` {expectedVersion} loaded a {artifact} engine from a release before 0.18, and the two must come from the same release, so csszyx stops.

help.version: install `@csszyx/core@{expectedVersion}`; it installs its platform package at the same version.
help.platform-package: install `@csszyx/core@{expectedVersion}`, and reinstall `{platformPackage}` if your lockfile holds it at another version.
help.unreported: install `@csszyx/core@{expectedVersion}`; it installs its platform package at the same version.
help.source: rebuild the engine from this checkout: `pnpm --filter @csszyx/core native:build` for native, `pnpm --filter @csszyx/core build` for wasm.

diagnostics.summary: A @csszyx/runtime at another version than the plugin that lowers for it.
diagnostics.text: `@csszyx/unplugin` {pluginVersion} found `@csszyx/runtime` {runtimeVersion} at `{runtimeDir}`, and the two must come from the same release, so the build stops.
diagnostics.help: install `@csszyx/runtime@{pluginVersion}`.

diagnostics.summary: A peer package csszyx needs that does not resolve from the project.
diagnostics.text: `{requiredBy}` reads templates with `{request}`, which does not resolve from it, so no template is read.
diagnostics.help: install `{install}` in the project.

diagnostics.summary: A project where generate-types finds no loadable Tailwind CSS v3.

text.absent: `csszyx generate-types` reads a Tailwind v3 config, and this project has no Tailwind installed.
text.wrong-major: `csszyx generate-types` reads a Tailwind v3 config, and this project has Tailwind {version}, which has no JavaScript config to read.
text.broken-entry: `csszyx generate-types` found Tailwind {version} but could not load its `resolveConfig` entry, so it cannot read the config.

help.absent: install `tailwindcss@3` as a dev dependency, such as `npm install -D tailwindcss@3`; on Tailwind v4 the theme lives in CSS under `@theme`, and this command is not needed.
help.wrong-major: declare the theme in CSS under `@theme`, which needs no generated types; to type a v3 config left over from a migration, run `npx -p tailwindcss@3 -p @csszyx/cli csszyx generate-types --config ./tailwind.config.js`.
help.broken-entry: reinstall it, such as `npm install --force tailwindcss@3`; if the error stays, report this csszyx bug at https://github.com/nguyennhutien/csszyx/issues with this message.

note.absent: `@csszyx/cli` lists Tailwind v3 as an optional peer, so installing the CLI does not install it.
note.wrong-major: `tailwind.config.js` and the `resolveConfig` helper this command calls were removed in Tailwind v4.

diagnostics.summary: An input to csszyx explain that is not one sz expression the build lowers.

text.not-one-expression: `{input}` is not one sz expression, so `csszyx explain` has nothing to resolve.
text.runtime-only: The build emits no classes for `{input}`, because `_sz()` resolves it at runtime.

help.not-one-expression: pass one object literal, such as `csszyx explain "{ p: 4, bg: 'blue-500' }"`.
help.runtime-only: write its values as literals to see the classes the build emits; a warning printed below, when there is one, names the value that needs the runtime.

diagnostics.summary: A Vue or Svelte file whose template sz has errors, each reported with its own code.
diagnostics.text: This file has {count} `sz` error(s), so the build stops.
diagnostics.help: fix each error listed below.

diagnostics.summary: A template sz value only known at runtime, which a template cannot resolve.
diagnostics.text: This `sz` value is only known at runtime, and a template has no csszyx runtime to resolve it, so it gets no class.
diagnostics.help: write the value as a literal, such as `{ p: 4 }`, or bind `class` or `style` yourself for a value that changes at runtime.
diagnostics.note: the attribute is left as written.

diagnostics.summary: A Vue or Svelte file its own compiler cannot parse, so no sz in it gets a class.

text.vue: Vue cannot parse this file, so no `sz` attribute in it gets a class.
text.svelte-quoted: Svelte cannot parse this file, so no `sz` attribute in it gets a class.
text.svelte-preprocess: Svelte cannot parse this file, so no `sz` attribute in it gets a class.

diagnostics.help: write the template in HTML, or bind `class` yourself in it.

diagnostics.summary: An installed Svelte older than 5, whose markup csszyx does not read.
diagnostics.text: Svelte {version} resolves here, and csszyx reads Svelte 5 markup only, so no `sz` attribute in this file gets a class.
diagnostics.help: install `svelte@5`.

diagnostics.note: the transform reported: {detail}.
